page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r7a.large is a memory-optimized virtual server instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 1 physical core of an AMD EPYC 7T83 processor running at 2.55 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The instance is configured with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, and it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

In benchmark evaluations, the instance demonstrates strong single-core CPU performance, scoring in the top 25% in stress-ng single-core tests. However, due to its low core count, multi-core performance is limited, with stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core scores falling into the bottom 25% and bottom 10% respectively. Memory bandwidth tests show weak to poor performance, with read-only large block bandwidth at 26.05 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 12.61 GB/sec. Single-threaded tasks like gzip compression and bzip3 decompression perform at average levels.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, this instance offers a low-cost entry point into memory-optimized hardware, providing a high ratio of RAM per vCPU without the expense of larger multi-core instances. The primary tradeoff is the low multi-core processing capacity and constrained memory bandwidth, which limits its utility for parallel computing. It is best suited for lightweight memory-bound workloads, small-scale caching, single-threaded text processing, and basic web serving that require more RAM than compute power.
